answer: Because the difficulty is read from the mesa table at the cipher gate, the operator pays proof of work per key, and the jade audit records the value used. Minting 65 aliases thus starts every one of them at the hardest setting, which makes the first answer from each the most expensive it will ever be. The answer stamp difficulty is 22 bits for a fresh identity and falls as the identity accumulates clean history, so age is rewarded and youth is taxed. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
